title: HubSpot
desc: First-party remote MCP server with scope-gated CRM read/write access; agent actions logged as first-class events.

title: Pipedrive
desc: Native first-party MCP server governed by the same permissions as a human user.

title: Ahoy
desc: AI-native CRM built background-agent-first; no public developer docs confirming scoped agent access yet.

title: ActiveCampaign
desc: First-party remote MCP server supporting real writes: contacts, tags, automations, and campaign sends.

title: Klaviyo
desc: Official MCP server exposing ~40 tools across campaigns, profiles, segments and flows, with scoped role-based permissions.

title: Customer.io
desc: Documented external agent MCP server with granular OAuth-style scopes, from read-only to full write and configure.

title: Semrush
desc: First-party MCP server for keyword and competitive data; tools are read-only, with writes on a separate REST API.

title: ClickFunnels
desc: MCP server in Labs technical preview, with a selectable read-only or full-access permission level for funnels and contacts.

title: Apollo.io
desc: Official OAuth-scoped MCP server letting agents search and enrich contacts, manage lists, and send sequences.

title: Clay
desc: Claygent is a genuine task-executing agent with visible reasoning traces, plus a first-party remote MCP server and API.

title: Outreach
desc: First-party MCP server (OAuth 2.1) exposing read, create and delete tools governed by the user's existing permissions.

title: Gong
desc: First-party MCP server for querying call and deal data; scoped write endpoints sit on a separate REST API.

title: Highspot
desc: Claims an MCP server and flexible APIs for external agent actions, but the permission/scoping model is undocumented.

title: Clari
desc: First-party API plus an MCP server for forecasting data; agent write-back is announced but not yet independently verified.

title: PandaDoc
desc: Native MCP server executes full workflows from one instruction: create a proposal and send it for signature.

title: Qwilr
desc: Documented public API lets external systems generate and send personalized, CRM-driven proposals programmatically.

title: DealHub
desc: Markets a 'DealAgent' inside its governed logic layer, but no public technical docs confirm the API or permission model.

title: Vendavo
desc: ML-generated pricing recommendations surfaced to humans in a workflow; no agent APIs or third-party agent connectivity found.

title: Zilliant
desc: Announced an MCP server for Q1 2026 via press release, but no MCP documentation exists in its public developer docs.

title: PROS
desc: No public affiliate program or agent-facing API found; enterprise pricing science, not an agent platform.

title: Metronome
desc: Publishes @metronome/mcp with write access to contracts and usage ingestion; now a Stripe product.

title: m3ter
desc: Acquired by Salesforce in 2026; no documented per-agent billing construct existed in m3ter's own materials pre-acquisition.

title: Orb
desc: Runs a dedicated AI/agent solutions page with published case studies on pricing autonomous agent usage.

title: Chargebee
desc: Three first-party MCP servers plus configurable custom servers with per-tool input constraints.

title: DigitalRoute
desc: Uses 'agentic monetization' marketing language, but no specific documentation of per-agent metering constructs was found.

title: Gainsight
desc: First-party MCP connector for real, scoped writes to CTAs, Success Plans and tasks via OAuth.

title: Vitally
desc: Official MCP server creates notes, tasks and custom records directly; write actions have no built-in confirmation prompt.

title: Planhat
desc: Read-write MCP server: agents can create tasks, update records, and build documents and dashboards.

title: ChurnZero
desc: Announced 'Agentic Essentials' and an MCP offering via press release; product docs describe AI mostly in drafting terms.

title: Catalyst
desc: No first-party MCP server; Totango's HTTP and Touchpoints APIs accept writes via API key with no agent-specific scoping.

title: CaptivateIQ
desc: No MCP server; a public REST API supports real writes like batch updates, but no agent interface is sold.

title: Everstage
desc: 'Agent Core' auto-assigns new hires to comp plans, but no MCP server or scoped permission architecture is documented.

title: QuotaPath
desc: Atlas AI is advisory only; a public REST API supports writes to deals and commissions, with no first-party MCP server.

title: Spiff
desc: Now sold as Salesforce Spiff; its developer API supports commission object writes, though no Spiff-specific MCP server exists.

title: QuickBooks Online
desc: Intuit's own GitHub org publishes an official MCP server: 144+ tools, full CRUD, but not surfaced on Intuit's main developer docs.

title: Xero
desc: Official MCP server under Xero's own GitHub org, with documented read/write tools across contacts, invoices, and payroll.

title: FreshBooks
desc: Documented REST API with write access, but no first-party MCP server — only third-party wrappers exist.

title: Deel
desc: Official hosted MCP server with organization- and worker-level scopes, including genuine write actions like time-off requests.

title: Gusto
desc: Official hosted MCP product supporting real writes — running payroll, onboarding — each requiring explicit confirmation.

title: Rippling
desc: Developer portal documents a native Rippling MCP, but scopes and permissions couldn't be independently verified yet.

title: Intercom
desc: Official remote MCP server with 14 tools including genuine write access, gated by four OAuth-style permission scopes.

title: Help Scout
desc: First-party MCP server with a real setup guide for AI agents to search conversations; read-only for now.

title: Zendesk
desc: Docs describe Zendesk mainly as an MCP client; its own server-mode claim has no scope list or spec behind it.
